subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw add native gateway/provider budget admission for per-agent spend limits, or should it expose only the plugin/API hooks needed for an external budget controller?
rationale: Current code can report cost and block whole runs, but the requested per-call spend enforcement changes config, provider dispatch, persistent state, and operator UX in ways automation should not choose without maintainer product direction.

options.title: Native Core Admission Layer
options.body: Add opt-in core budget config plus durable gateway/provider admission, reservations/refunds, receipts, status/doctor surfaces, and docs so spending can be refused before provider calls.

options.title: Plugin/API-First Boundary
options.body: Keep budget policy outside core but add a narrow pre-model-call hook and accounting contract that external budget plugins can implement safely.

options.title: External Controls Only
options.body: Close the native request and document that users should rely on external billing proxies or provider-side limits, accepting that OpenClaw will not enforce per-agent budgets itself.

recommendation.title: Native Core Admission Layer
recommendation.body: Add opt-in core budget config plus durable gateway/provider admission, reservations/refunds, receipts, status/doctor surfaces, and docs so spending can be refused before provider calls.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available routing candidate because the issue spans usage-cost reporting, gateway/provider policy, and product-level runtime guardrails.
